text:
Alex R: Quick check — I want to run a short sampling job on staging to validate the TTFT / tok/s / p95 panels before the next release. Who can own the perf run today?

Mari V: I can kick it off in ~30m. Is this the same sampling config we used last month?

Alex R: Similar but tweaked: lower seq length to 512 and 10% sampling across different batch sizes. Command I was thinking:```./perf-run --model=redwood-gpt-small --seq=512 --qps=40 --duration=20m --sample=0.1 --batches=32,64,128```

Cheng L: Heads up — make sure profiler-bot is enabled so we capture kernel timelines. Also flag whether we want ingress-queue time included in TTFT.

Samir: For dashboards we currently define TTFT as time from request accepted by the ingress layer to first token emitted by the model. That includes queue time. Do we want a runtime-only TTFT (pop-to-first-token) as well?

Nina: I recommend both. Runtime-only helps isolate kernel regressions. Ingress-inclusive aligns with user-facing SLOs. Two panels: TTFT_ingress and TTFT_runtime.

Mari V: perf-run started. profiler-bot enabled. ETA ~20m. Posting initial config:```sampling:10%
seq_len:512
qps:40
batch_sizes:[32,64,128]
model_variant:quant4x```

profiler-bot: profiler started on pool-staging-3 · collecting kv-cache / kernel events · trace_id=tr-1765432100-a1

Alex R: Great — when you have results, include per-shard tok/s and per-request p95. We need to check if our current aggregation (median of p95s across shards) is deceiving. Suggest arithmetic mean of per-shard p95 weighted by request count.

Cheng L: Agree on weighted mean. Also log the sample size per shard. If a shard has <20 samples, mark as low-confidence.

Mari V: Got a quick summary (first 6m):
```
overall_tok_s: 1800
TTFT_ingress_p95: 142ms
TTFT_runtime_p95: 98ms
p95_first_token_by_shard: [120, 95, 210, 130]
samples_per_shard: [250, 230, 18, 240]
```

Samir: Looks like shard 3 is low-sample and an outlier (210ms). Can we repro with a focused run on that shard? @Cheng L can you allocate a targeted run on the same machine class?

Cheng L: Yep, I can repro. Kicking a 10m focused job on that shard only. Will also collect nvprof call stacks.

Nina: Dashboard changes we should make before merging:
- Add TTFT_runtime and TTFT_ingress side-by-side with the same time window
- Show token-rate heatmap by shard
- Add sample-count overlay and a low-confidence badge if samples < 50
- Tooltip with aggregation method (weighted mean vs median)

Alex R: Also add a note in the panel description about how we compute tok/s (tokens emitted per second / per active GPU). Make sure we normalize by effective concurrency (in-flight reqs) not just QPS.

Cheng L: Focused job done. profiler-bot uploaded traces: trace_id=tr-1765432100-b2. Preliminary kernel stall identified during kv-cache restore on that shard. Looks like a memcpy fallback happened.

Samir: Oof — memcpy fallback would explain the p95 spike. Can you attach stack and the small log excerpt?

Cheng L: Log snippet:```[2026-07-16T14:12:43Z] kv_restore: fallback memcpy used (expected async memcpy) on gpu0, bytes=24MB, latency=32ms```

Mari V: Thanks. I'll update the dashboard PR with the new panels and the low-confidence badge. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-dashboards/pull/498 — pinging @Alex R and @Cheng L for quick CR.

Alex R: Reviewing now. If we land the dashboard change, let's also add an automated alert: TTFT_runtime_p95 increases by >30% over 1h and sample_count >=100. Otherwise we get noisy alerts from small samples.

Nina: I'll add the alert rule and a muted window for staging.

profiler-bot: trace artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-profiles/tr-1765432100-a1 and tr-1765432100-b2

Samir: Next steps summary:
- Cheng to file a microfix for memcpy path / follow with kernel change (ASSIGNED)
- Mari to finish dashboard PR and add sample-count badge (ASSIGNED)
- Nina to add the alert rule and mute staging noise (ASSIGNED)
- Alex to approve dashboard PR and merge after Cheng confirms fix

Alex R: Thanks everyone — good coordination. Please ping if anything blocks. :thumbsup:
